questions.q: How many different places in Power Query can you use to change a column's data type?
options: Four — Home ribbon, Transform ribbon, the column header icon, and the right-click menu
Only one, the right-click menu
Two — Home ribbon and Transform ribbon only
It depends entirely on the data source type
questions.explain: The same Data type choice is available from the Home tab, the Transform tab, the icon on the column heading itself, and the right-click "Change Type" menu.

questions.q: A column of dates written as "22/01/2020" fails to convert to Date type with a DataFormat.Error. What's the most likely cause?
options: A locale mismatch — the dates are day/month/year, but Power Query assumed month/day/year
The file is corrupted
Power Query doesn't support the Date data type
The column needs to be converted to Text first
questions.explain: "22/01/2020" can't be month/day/year since there's no 22nd month — the data was written in day/month/year (UK) format while Power Query assumed the computer's default region's format.

questions.q: How do you fix a date conversion that's failing due to a locale mismatch?
options: Right-click the column, choose Change Type, then "Using Locale," and specify the correct source region
Delete the column and re-enter the data manually
Switch your computer's Windows region settings
It can't be fixed — you must leave the column as Text
questions.explain: "Change type with locale" lets you specify both the target data type and the locale the source values were actually written in, so Power Query interprets them correctly.

questions.q: What does the small icon on the left of a column heading indicate?
options: The column's current data type
Whether the column has any errors
Whether the column is sorted
The column's original source file format
questions.explain: Each data type (Text, Whole Number, Date, etc.) has its own icon shown on the column heading, so you can tell a column's type at a glance.

questions.q: What should you check for after converting a column to a new data type?
options: Any [Error] cells, which indicate values that couldn't be parsed
Whether the column changed color
Whether the file size increased
Nothing — Power Query conversions never fail silently or visibly
questions.explain: A failed conversion shows [Error] in the affected cells rather than crashing or failing silently — always scan for these before moving on to the next step.
